The disruption in service of any alternative method does not preclude the City Council or other legislative body
from taking further action on an agenda item.

Submitting Comments Prior to Public Meeting: Members of the public may choose to submit comments
electronically for consideration by the City Council or other City Legislative Body by sending them to the City
Clerk/Secretary at athompson@cityofinglewood.org, and Deputy City Clerk at aallen@cityofinglewood.org. To

 comments prior to 8:00 a.m. the day of the meeting, and in the body of the email, please identify the agenda

Boulevard, First Floor, Inglewood City Hall, Inglewood, CA 90301 or via email to
athompson@cityofinglewood.org and aallen@cityofinglewood.org no later than 24 hours prior to the scheduled

Inglewood, California
  December 5, 2023

  The City Council of the City of Inglewood, California held a regular meeting on Tuesday,
  December 5, 2023, in the Council Chambers in City Hall of said City.

  Following the Pledge of Allegiance to the flag of our Country, Mayor Butts called the City
  Council into joint session with the Successor Agency, Housing Authority and Joint Powers
  Authority at the hour of 2:03 p.m.
  The City Clerk/Successor Agency Secretary/Housing Authority Secretary/Joint Powers
  Authority Secretary announced the presence of a quorum as follows:

  Present:  Mayor/Successor Agency Chairman/Housing Authority
  Chairman/ Joint Powers Authority Chairman Butts,
  Council Members/Successor Agency Members/Housing
  Authority Members/ Joint Powers Authority Members
  Padilla, Morales, Faulk; and
  Absent:  Council Member/Successor Agency Member/Housing
  Authority Member/Joint Powers Authority Member Gray.
  City/Successor Agency/Housing Authority/ Joint Powers Authority officials and personnel
  present were as follows:
  Aisha L. Thompson  City Clerk/Secretary*
  Artie Fields  City Manager/ Executive Director*
  Ken Campos  City Attorney/General Counsel*
  Louis Atwell  Assistant City Manager/Public Works Director
  Angela Allen  Deputy City Clerk

  * Serves as indicated for the Successor Agency, Housing Authority, and Joint Powers
  Authority.

  MAYOR BUTTS COMMENTS. Mayor Butts announced that the City Council Meeting
  will be adjourned in memory of Council Member Gray’s life partner Leonard Tibbs.

  PUBLIC COMMENTS – AGENDA ITEMS. Mayor/Successor Agency
  Chairman/Housing Authority Chairman/ Joint Powers Authority Chairman Butts inquired
  if there were any persons present who wished to address the City Council/Successor
  Agency/Housing Authority/ Joint Powers Authority on any item on the Agendas, other than
  the public hearing.

  Speaker (Name Unknown) spoke concerning Agenda Item No. PH-1, and was advised to
  save his public comments during the public hearing to address his concerns.

142.9  PAYMENT OF WARRANTS AND BILLS. It was moved by Council Member
  /Successor Agency Member / Housing Authority Member Morales, and seconded by
  Council Member/Successor Agency Member/Housing Authority Member Padilla that the
  demands presented to the City Council/Successor Agency/Housing Authority dated
  December 1, 2023, in the amount of $5,892,223.43 and dated November 17, 2023, in the
  amount of $6,691,289.67 are hereby allowed, and the City Clerk/Successor Agency
  Secretary/Housing Authority Secretary is hereby authorized to certify upon said registers
  that said demands are so approved. The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members/Successor Agency Members/Housing Authority Members
  Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor/Successor Agency Chairman/Housing
  Authority Chairman Butts;
  Noes: None; and
  Absent: Council Member/Successor Agency Member/Housing Authority Member Gray.
 December 5, 2023

301  PUBLIC HEARING HELD – CATEGORICAL EXEMPTION (EA-CE-2023-031)
  AFFIRMED; ORDINANCE NO. 24-02 INTRODUCED – APPROVAL OF ZONING
  CODE AMENDMENT NO. 23-00006 (ZCA23-00006) ESTABLISHING
  REGULATIONS FOR ACCESSORY DWELLING UNITS IN CHAPTER 12 OF
  THE INGLEWOOD MUNICIPAL CODE, CITYWIDE. The City Clerk announced
  that the next scheduled matter was a public hearing to consider introduction of an ordinance
  approving Zoning Code Amendment No. 23-00006 (ZCA23-00006) to establish regulations
  for Accessory Dwelling Units in Chapter 12 of the Inglewood Municipal Code, Citywide,
  that notice was given in the time, form, and manner as required by law, an affidavit was on
  file, and no communications were received.

  Mayor Butts inquired if there were any persons present that wished to address the City
  Council on this matter.

  Speaker (Name Unknown) stated that it was brought to his attention that the public
  hearing to modify the allowed ADU construction was because single-family homeowners
  had problems with two-story ADUs compromising their backyard privacy. He also stated he was
  a long-time residential designer and 30-year homeowner in Inglewood. The  speaker
  opposed the Zoning Code Amendment because he felt two-story homes do the  same thing as
  two-story ADUs, which look into neighboring properties' backyards.  Additionally,  he
  addressed his clients interested in building and maintaining their ADUs above their garages.
  He also addressed that one-story ADUs take away onsite parking, and it’s unfair to group
  everyone together because multi-family homes have different  issues than single-family
  homes. The speaker mentioned that his duplex backs onto a  commercial lot, so his two-
  story duplex faces his neighbor's backyard. Furthermore, the  speaker  also  mentioned
  suburban areas, the square footage of their lots, and not being  fixated on his neighbor's
  backyard because it would cause problems. He discussed large  apartment complexes not
  having backyards, and one of his clients is trying to maintain  his carport and build an ADU
  above it to maintain parking. Finally, the speaker also  discussed the rippling number of
  issues if everyone has to put their ADUs on ground level and cautioned the Council to consider
  that and having a 60-day or 3-month period for projects already in process won’t find out at the
  last minute.

  Council Member Morales left the dais at the hour of 2:08 p.m.

  Javana Grimes, Custody Officer for the Los Angeles County Sheriff's Department and the
  new owner of the UPS Store located at 112 S. Market Street. She thanked the Council for
  all they had done for the City and said she looked forward to embracing the change. The
  speaker stated that if not for the reassurance of the City, she wouldn't be able to open the
  UPS Store that she loves so much. She discussed the UPS Store's services and franchise
  opportunities. Additionally, she added that she wanted to encourage more businesses to
  entrust the City of Inglewood and Mayor Butts for laying the foundation to take chances, build,
  flourish, and succeed. Finally, the speaker mentioned the Grand Opening in mid- January and
  hoped the Council would be there to support it.

  Council Member Morales returned to the dais at the hour of 2:10 p.m.

  Speaker (Name Unknown) discussed items not on the Agenda and was advised to save her
  public comment for the end of the meeting so she could address her concerns.

  Mayor Butts closed the public comments portion at the hour of 2:12 p.m.

  Artie Fields, City Manager, presented the Staff Report dated December 5, 2023.

  Bernard McCrumby, Jr., Acting Planner Manager, presented a brief oral report regarding
  Accessory Dwelling Units and Junior Accessory Dwelling Units.
